step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes OLX Autos' internal developer platform. It starts with an 'ExternalUser' accessing the 'Orion portal', which first resolves DNS via 'Route 53'. The request is then routed to an 'ALB' and subsequently to 'EKS', which orchestrates application pods running on 'EC2' spot instances. For resilient job processing, the application within 'EKS' sends events to 'SNS', which then publishes messages to 'SQS'. New or replaced application pods consume these messages from 'SQS' to ensure continuous processing and state consistency.

graph.notes: This architecture describes the OLX Autos' internal developer platform, 'Orion portal'. It leverages AWS EKS running on 100% EC2 Spot Instances for cost optimization, with SNS and SQS for resilient job orchestration and handling of spot terminations. nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: End-user interacting with the Orion portal.

nodes.name: Route 53
nodes.notes: Used for DNS resolution for the Orion portal.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Application Load Balancer, routes incoming traffic to the EKS cluster.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service, orchestrates the application pods. Manages workload and interacts with messaging services for job handling.

nodes.name: Spot Instances
nodes.notes: Underlying compute resources for EKS, utilizing 100% EC2 Spot Instances for cost efficiency.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Amazon Simple Notification Service, receives events when microservice provisioning jobs are triggered.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Amazon Simple Queue Service, stores messages for unfinished jobs, allowing new pods to pick up tasks after spot terminations.

edges.notes: User accesses Orion portal, triggering DNS resolution.
Route 53 resolves DNS to the Application Load Balancer.
ALB forwards requests to the Kubernetes pods managed by EKS.
EKS orchestrates and deploys application pods onto EC2 Spot Instances.
Application (within EKS/EC2 context) sends an event to SNS when a microservice provisioning job is triggered.
SNS publishes the job event message to SQS.
New or replaced EKS pods (application) consume messages from SQS to resume or finish pending jobs.
